problem.claim: Efficiently learn and model long sequences, including long-horizon forecasting.

gap.claim: The authors contrast LinOSS with prior state-space models that rely heavily on restrictive parameterizations.

contributions.claim: LinOSS, a linear oscillatory state-space model based on forced harmonic oscillators and stable discretization with fast associative parallel scans.

The authors report stable dynamics with only a nonnegative diagonal state matrix, universality for continuous causal operators, and symmetry-preserving time reversibility under an implicit-explicit discretization.
The authors report consistent outperformance of state-of-the-art sequence models across mid-range to very long-range classification, regression, and long-horizon forecasting tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish LinOSS by combining oscillator-based dynamics, a less restrictive stability condition, universality, and preservation of time-reversibility symmetry.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that LinOSS outperforms Mamba and LRU by nearly 2× on a sequence-modeling task with sequence length 50k.
The authors report consistent outperformance across a broad set of time-series classification, regression, and forecasting tasks.
The authors state theoretical results for stability, universality, and symmetry preservation under the specified discretizations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Introduces LinOSS for efficient learning on long sequences, motivated by cortical dynamics and forced harmonic oscillators.
Uses stable discretization and fast associative parallel scans to obtain the state-space model.
States stability, universality, and time-reversibility properties of LinOSS and its discretizations.
Links these properties to efficient long-range interaction modeling and stable, accurate long-horizon forecasting.
Reports broad task-level gains, including nearly 2× over Mamba and LRU at sequence length 50k.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns architectural choices with formal properties: stable discretization supports stability, while an implicit-explicit discretization preserves time-reversibility symmetry.

lessons.interpretation: A method description can be more informative when each design choice is connected to a specific claimed guarantee.
lessons.application: When presenting a new sequence model, pair each numerical or architectural mechanism with the exact theoretical property it is intended to preserve.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the claimed property has no formal statement or when the design-property link is only speculative.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide datasets, baselines beyond Mamba and LRU for the 50k result, statistical variation, or detailed metrics.
The conditions and proof details for stability, universality, and exact time-reversibility are not specified.
The basis for the reported consistency across tasks and the meaning of nearly 2× are not detailed.
